t: This is the Cheshire Cheese, a Grade II listed pub on the corner of Little Essex Street and Milford Lane, in Temple. A tavern has stood on this site since the sixteenth century, and a pub of this name has been recorded here since at least 1791. The building you see was rebuilt or extensively remodelled in 1928 to designs by Nowell Parr, an architect best known for pubs in west London. Inside, the interior is on CAMRA's National Inventory of Historic Pub Interiors, rated three stars for outstanding national historic importance.
